title: Predictive eviction crediting and tenant handshake for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Patel
description: PRD for a predictive eviction-crediting system plus a tenant-handshake protocol to improve Dedicated capacity fairness and graceful degradation during transient overloads. Introduces tenant 'burst credit' ledger, short-term predictive eviction windows, and an API/console handshake that allows customers to signal latency-tolerance and acceptable fallback models. Intended to reduce noisy preemption, surface clearer billing and SLA signals, and enable deterministic canary rollouts when capacity pressure spikes.
background: We currently handle Dedicated pool contention with hard preemption and coarse soft-evict heuristics. This causes two issues: (1) noisy single-tenant preempts during short spikes that trigger customer incidents, and (2) limited ability to coordinate graceful fallbacks with customer applications (they can't signal acceptable model degradations or latency envelopes). Several customers have requested better burst semantics and clearer observable credits for burst usage. This initiative builds on existing reserved pool and soft-eviction work but changes the model to be predictive-credit based with an explicit tenant handshake API.
goals: Define a tenant burst-credit ledger (predictive credits) with clear accrual and depletion rules
Implement a tenant-handshake API so customers can declare acceptable fallback tiers and latency envelopes per route
Reduce involuntary preemption incidents by 50% in first 3 months after rollout for targeted tenants
Expose console UI and API endpoints for credits, forecasted eviction windows, and billing impact
Provide deterministic canary rollout strategy that leverages credit forecasts to avoid cascade evictions
non_goals: Changing long-term reservation accounting (monthly committed capacity) — this PRD only affects transient burst handling
Replacing existing SLA/legal contract language — billing/legal will be separate
Major runtime kernel changes (e.g., new attention kernels) — we will rely on current serving runtime interfaces
user_stories: As a tenant, I want to see my burst credit balance and forecast so I can predict if an upcoming spike will risk preemption
As an operator, I want the system to predict eviction windows and throttle low-priority traffic to avoid full pool preemption
As a PM, I want an API so customers can declare acceptable fallback models and max-latency per route to enable graceful degradation
As a support engineer, I want clear audit logs explaining why a request was preempted or soft-evicted (credit depletion vs policy)
requirements: Design a credit ledger with accrual (steady-state low utilization) and predictive accrual from past usage (lookback window configurable, default 24h)
Credits must have TTL semantics (default 48h) and a configurable max cap per tenant
Predictive eviction algorithm must run every 10s per pool and publish a 60s forecasted eviction probability per tenant
Tenant-handshake API: POST /v1/dedicated/handshake with body fields 'route_id', 'fallback_models' (ordered list), 'max_latency_ms', 'allow_degraded_quality' (boolean), 'billing_ack' (boolean)
Console: Show credit balance, forecast chart, last 10 eviction events, and a test 'simulate spike' button for tenants with admin access
Audit log entries for any eviction event must include: reason (credit-depletion|policy-preempt|zonal-failure), credit_balance_before, forecasted_eviction_prob
Backward-compatible: tenants that do not call handshake get default fallback policy (strict preemption)
APIs and UI must be behind RBAC and respect existing VPC/private settings
Create flag rollout (runtime config) to enable predictive eviction for select zones/accounts before cluster-wide rollout
acceptance_criteria: Credit ledger exists and is readable via GET /v1/dedicated/credits/{tenant_id} and returns fields 'balance', 'cap', 'ttl_expiry'
Tenant-handshake accepts and persists configuration; requests with handshake must be honored by routing decisions within 15s
Eviction probability forecasts are emitted to our metrics pipeline (metric: dedicated.eviction_forecast_by_tenant) at 10s cadence
Console surfaces credit balance and forecast chart for the tenant in the Dedicated -> Capacity view
Incidents: For the 10 tenants in the initial canary, involuntary hard preemptions due to pool pressure reduce by >=50% versus baseline over 30 days
All eviction-related audit logs are searchable in the SLO dashboard and link to the tenant's credit history
Integration tests: simulated spike (10x request rate for 90s) degrades traffic using declared fallback_models and respects max_latency_ms for 95% of requests in the test
Security: handshake and credit endpoints pass SAST/DAST and respect SSO RBAC rules
Rollout: Feature flag gated; canary rollout to 5% of customers in week 1, 25% in week 2, full rollout after safety review
rollout_plan: Start with an internal dogfooding phase for Redwood platform teams (2 weeks), then canary 5% customers (week 1) focusing on tenants with medium credit usage. Monitor eviction incidents, credit anomalies, and customer feedback. Expand to 25% (week 2) then 100% after 2-week observation window and postmortem. Provide a kill-switch to revert to previous soft-evict heuristic immediately. Coordinate with Sales/CS for customers in Dedicated who must opt-in to handshake mode.
metrics: p95/max request latency for routes with handshake vs without
risks: Incorrect credit accrual policy could unfairly favor noisy tenants or starve low-usage tenants
Forecasting algorithm false positives/negatives could cause unnecessary throttles or missed preemptions
Billing confusion if credits are misinterpreted as free capacity — need clear console labels and billing documentation
Operational complexity: more telemetry to ingest and retain; possible cost increase
Latency cost: predictive loop (10s cadence) must be efficient; otherwise it could add CPU pressure to control plane
dependencies: runtime: expose per-tenant utilization metrics and ability to accept external credit signals (ENG-50412)
console: new UI surfaces and sim button (DES-21034)
billing: mapping credits to invoice view and documentation (FIN-9811)
security: SSO/RBAC review on handshake endpoints (SEC-1158)
observability: metrics pipeline capacity and alerting for eviction_forecast metric (ENG-51200)
decisions: Use a hybrid accrual model: base accrual (time-weighted) + usage-backed predictive top-up based on 24h lookback
Keep defaults conservative: tenants not opting into handshake fall back to existing strict preemption
Eviction forecast window set to 60s with 10s cadence as a trade-off between responsiveness and stability
Credits are cosmetic from a billing standpoint initially (informational). After 3 months, evaluate conversion to billable burst credits if customer demand and legal approve
open_questions: What is the exact accrual formula (lookback weights)? Need Eng + Research for a proposal
Should credits be transferable across routes within a tenant? (multi-route tenants may want aggregate view)
Billing: can we offer a 'paid burst' product tied to this ledger in Phase 2? Finance/legal input required
What default fallback_models should we provide in the SDK/console for common inference stacks?
